messages:
Maria (AE): Hey team — EdgeML wants to run an end-to-end POC this week focused on tail latency and burst cost. They're particularly worried about 95/99th latencies during traffic spikes and how that maps to monthly spend. Can SRE/SE own the load plan and a quick cost estimate?
Devon (SRE): I can own the load plan. Quick Qs: model size (float vs quant), max seq len, expected avg tokens per request, and whether KV/prefix cache is safe to use.
Maria (AE): They're serving a small instruction-following model, ~7B fp16 in our catalog. Typical seq len 256, avg 120 tokens output. They'd like to test steady 500 qps with 30s spikes to 2k qps. Budget target: keep incremental cost under $6k/month if possible.
Ryan (Sales Eng): Draft plan below. Devon please sanity-check and we'll run a smoke tonight.
Ryan (Sales Eng): LOAD PLAN:
- Warmup: 5m ramp from 50 -> 500 qps
- Steady-state: 30m at 500 qps (measure p50/p95/p99, token/sec)
- Spike test: 3 x 30s bursts to 2000 qps spaced 2m apart
- Cold-cache run: single long-request batch after routing to a fresh node
- Repeat with prefix caching enabled
- Capture infra metrics (GPU util, mem, network), request traces and token counts
Devon (SRE): Looks good. Will use our benchmark harness (vegeta wrapper) to simulate concurrency. Example load command we plan to use:
```
vegeta attack -rate=500 -duration=30m -targets=targets.txt | vegeta report -type=json > steady500.json
```
Will set up separate target sets for spike and cold-cache runs.
Devon (SRE): API config snippet (for infra team):
```
POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>, X-Model: redwood-7b-fp16
Body: {"input":"<prompt>", "max_tokens":120, "stream":false}
```
Devon (SRE): Observability: capture p50/p95/p99, 95/99 token-per-second throughput, queue depth, and token cost. Also set an alert threshold p99 > 800ms.
Maria (AE): Customer asked about pricing math — can we translate token/sec into $/month for their traffic profile?
Ryan (Sales Eng): Quick estimate: at current hosted rates, 500 qps * 120 tokens * 30s avg per minute ~ (calc) — I'll post a clean calc after run, but rough incremental of ~ $3.5k/mo for steady 500 qps; spikes add variance.
Priya (Security): Heads-up on enterprise blockers: customer requires KMS-managed keys + audit logs + SOC2 attestation. Also they asked if traffic can stay within their VPC (private deployment) for production. For POC they're OK with hosted if logs and retention answers are provided.
Maria (AE): Ok we'll need Priya to provide the security Qs for the questionnaire; that might be a gating item for Dedicated/Private.
Priya (Security): I'll draft answers tonight. For the POC, we can use short-lived keys and provide a data retention statement. If they need VPC, that becomes a Dedicated deployment discussion and will affect cost estimates.
Devon (SRE): Ran a quick smoke just now (night run). Preliminary results: steady 500 qps p95=180ms, p99=420ms, tail spikes during bursts hit ~780ms. Cold-cache p95 jumped to ~1.1s on one node. Attached logs in gs://redwood-poc/edge-1718123456 (infra-bot uploaded).
infra-bot: upload completed: gs://redwood-poc/edge-1718123456/steady500.json
Devon (SRE): Observed what looks like KV cache cold-miss behavior during the first burst. Enabling prefix caching reduced cold p95 to 420ms in a repeat run.
Ryan (Sales Eng): That's promising — can we get a short writeup for the customer summarizing: steady-state latencies, tail behavior during spikes, what changes with prefix cache, and an estimated monthly cost with and without dedicated private nodes?
Devon (SRE): I'll write a 1-page summary and include the vegeta commands, raw numbers, and recommendation: for predictable tail under heavy bursts recommend either Reserved Dedicated capacity or autoscale with warmup buffer + prefix caching.
Maria (AE): Customer also asked whether we can guarantee no data egress to other tenants during POC. Priya?
Priya (Security): For hosted POC we can guarantee logical isolation and no cross-tenant access. For strict physical isolation they need Dedicated. I'll add clear language in the security responses.
Maria (AE): Great. Next steps: Devon to post the summarized run results + cost calc by EOD tomorrow. Priya to send security Q&A. Ryan to prepare a short deck comparing Hosted vs Dedicated for tail-latency SLAs and monthly costs. I'll coordinate timing with the customer's engineers for the full run on Thursday morning PST. @Devon please mark ownership. :thumbsup:
Devon (SRE): Marking ownership — will push the summary by EOD tomorrow and schedule the longer run on Thu 09:00 PST.
Maria (AE): Thanks team — this one matters to the deal.
